newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude prices lower, LLS diff edges up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude prices lower, LLS diff edges up.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes prices remained lower in early afternoon trading Monday as many buyers remained on the sidelines.
Outright crude prices traded as low as $19.28 and were about unchanged from late last week just before the 1515 EDT close of NYMEX trading at $19.50/60.
Domestic grade differentials were largely unchanged, though Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James remained fairly firm due to the tight arbitrage with the North Sea, traders said.
"It's a cat and mouse game. The refiners are waiting for Iraq to kick in and push it lower. But if there's a hitch it'll go back above $20," said a cash crude broker.
The market is waiting for the delivery of the distribution plan by the Iraqi government to the United Nations under their "oil-for-food" deal in order to see a resumption of Iraq's crude oil exports.

The U.N. Coordinator in Iraq said last week that the U.N.'s part of the plant, dealing with the three northern governates outside of Baghdad's control, was complete and Bagdad was working on last details in order to incorporate those elements.
The plan is expected to be received by the U.N. sometime this week but has not yet been submitted, the U.N. said Monday.
Meanwhile, U.S. refiners were expecting lower prices and had plenty of crude on offer, traders said.
Midland/West Texas Intermediate traded at a 30 cent disount to benchmark Cushing/WTI, hardly changed from late last week.

The lower WTI/Brent differential, due to Brent sales to the Far East and a lower August availability, pushed Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James, Brent's closest domestic competitor, a few cents higher. LLS traded at a 19 cents and 21 cents premium to WTI on Monday.
